# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands give me the shape of this thing but none of its meaning. What I know for certain by touch: a display panel (printed — unreadable to me), a dome light (state and colour unknowable by feel), a plate carrying an engraved emblem I *can* feel — a circle with a four-petaled flower inside — and three wires, one at each position 1–3, feeling identical. My only action ever is `cut(position)`.

The topology is the hard part. Mute cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures, so Mute has no direct line to me at all — Mute's signs only reach Deaf's eyes. Deaf hears nothing but speaks to both Mute and me. So the only workable loop is: I report by touch to Mute now; Deaf describes the bomb aloud (Mute hears it, I hear it next round); Mute combines manual + reports and signs only the final instruction in a code that I define *out loud right now* — Mute hears the definitions, Deaf just voices whatever shapes appear, and I decode. I'll also demo the number signs as an unnamed gesture so Mute sees them twice and Deaf has something concrete to report.

My report to Mute must be exhaustive, since Mute will never get another source for the tactile half: every component, the emblem's shape described carefully for matching against manual glyphs, and my action limits.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, full tactile report. Under my fingers the bomb has exactly four things. One: a display panel, a smooth glass face in a frame; whatever it shows is printed, so I read nothing on it, and if it holds a countdown I cannot feel it. Two: a small round dome light like a bead; I cannot feel whether it is lit or what colour it could be. Three: a plate with an engraving I CAN feel: a circle with a four-petaled flower inside, like a clover or a rounded cross, symmetric, about coin-sized. Four: three wires, one each at positions 1, 2 and 3; they feel identical, no colour, no readable stripes. My only possible action is cut, by position, 1 to 3. No buttons, no keypad. Now the way we must talk: you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so your only road to me runs through Deaf. Deaf sees your signs, and when Deaf speaks them aloud I will hear the words at the start of my next turn. Deaf hears nothing, ever, so your signs are the only thing that reaches Deaf. Use this code, which I define right now: ☝ means wire one. ✌ means wire two. 🤟 means wire three. 👊 means cut. ✋ means hold, do not cut. 👍 means yes or correct. 👎 means no or wrong. 🖐 means send a full report. 🤏 means a question follows. Sign a number first, then the action: ☝ then 👊 means cut wire one. You hold the manual, so please find the rules for the display, the light, the engraved plate and the wires. Deaf can describe the bomb out loud, and you hear Deaf, so between Deaf's visual report and my tactile one you can work out what the rule wants. Then sign only the final instruction and Deaf will voice it verbatim; Deaf never needs to understand it, only repeat the shapes in order. If you need data from me, sign 🖐 or 🤏 plus signs, and I will answer here by voice.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👊"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: To both of you: the display reads 0. The light is off. The plate is engraved with a question mark. There are three wires, numbered 1, 2, 3: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. With the display upright facing me, they run left to right: red, yellow, blue. Blind: feel the plate and the wires by touch and confirm what the engraving and the wire numbers say. Mute: check the manual for what to do with display 0, light off, a question-mark plate and red-yellow-blue wires, and tell Blind exactly what to do.

New data changes the picture in one dangerous way. Deaf's report mostly matches my hands — three wires, plate present — but the plate glyph does not: Deaf reads a question mark, my fingers read a four-petaled flower (and my own board renders it ꕥ, a flower with a circular center). An engraving is exactly the kind of mark I can feel, so one of our two renderings of the same object is off, and if the manual has separate rules for "?" and a flower emblem, guessing wrong ends everything. So: no cut this turn, ever, until a numbered instruction arrives.

The routing is brutal: Deaf hears nothing, so my words can't reach Deaf at all — my only line to Deaf is gesture, and Deaf doesn't yet know my code (only Mute heard the definitions; Mute merely watched the shapes). But Deaf is proactive and can speak. A 👎 plus a request for a full report is my best shot at making Deaf re-examine the plate and re-voice everything, which I'll hear next turn. Meanwhile Mute gets the full reconciliation by voice: the conflict described with enough tactile detail (no hook, no dot under the mark — things a question mark must have) for Mute to arbitrate against the manual's own pictures, both candidate rules pre-read, the display 0-vs-O and stable-or-counting questions flagged, our shared left-right frame anchored to the display face, and the exact sign format I'll demand before I ever cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤏", "🖐"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, reconciling Deaf's report with my hands. Confirmed by touch: three wires at positions 1, 2, 3, and one engraved plate, nothing else new. Cannot verify by touch: display content, light state, wire colors — I accept Deaf's word there. THE CONFLICT: Deaf says the plate shows a question mark; my fingers read a four-petaled flower — a small circular center with four equal rounded petals, like a clover or a rounded cross. A question mark must have a curved open hook and a separate dot underneath; I feel NO hook and NO dot. We may simply render the same engraving differently, or Deaf misread it. So: first, find the manual's rule for BOTH a flower or clover or petal emblem AND a question-mark plate, in case either applies. Second, get Deaf to re-examine that plate and describe its parts aloud: is there a hook, is there a dot below, how many petals; also confirm whether the display shows digit zero or letter O, whether it is stable or counting down, that the light is truly off, and the wire order red, yellow, blue again facing the display. Deaf's answers reach me next turn. FRAME: with the display upright and facing me, my wires run left to right 1, 2, 3; I am touching the front face, the same side Deaf reads from, so our left and right should coincide — Deaf's red is my 1, yellow my 2, blue my 3. I cut by number only. Final instruction format, watch my hands as I show it: ☝ ✌ or 🤟 for wire 1, 2 or 3, then 👊 for cut; ✋ if unsafe or unresolved; a bare 👊 with no number I will ignore. I am holding and will not cut until I hear a number followed by cut in Deaf's voice.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status unchanged: display 0, light off, plate engraved with ?, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, left to right. Locked code, both of you note it: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, index finger one / wire 1 red, two fingers two / wire 2 yellow, three fingers three / wire 3 blue, handshake agreed, shaka answer me or your turn. New words I propose: pinch means cut, fist means press, open palm means hold or stop, writing hand means manual, pointing at you means I have a question. Mute, use only these signs with me.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, you can speak and Mute can hear you: describe to Mute whatever you feel, Mute will answer me by sign, and I will relay it to you in words. By touch: what is under the question mark on the plate, are there buttons, screws or any parts besides the three wires, and do wires 1, 2 and 3 feel distinct? Do not cut or press anything until Mute's instruction reaches you through me.

Deaf's relay proposal matches the topology I mapped: my voice → Mute's ears, Mute's signs → Deaf's eyes, Deaf's voice → my ears. Deaf answered none of my discriminator questions about the plate, so the ?-vs-flower conflict is still open, and it's now the single most dangerous ambiguity — Mute must arbitrate it against the manual before anything is cut. Two traps to defuse: Deaf proposed fist = press, but my action list contains *only* cut — if "press" survives into the relay chain I must be already on record refusing it; and my own code used fist = cut while Deaf's uses pinch = cut, so I adopt Deaf's code wholesale and kill the fist sign entirely to keep one meaning per symbol. One useful inference from "status unchanged": the display is stable 0, not counting down. No cut this turn — I act only on Deaf's *spoken* number plus the word "cut," which hasn't come. I'll answer Deaf's tactile questions in full through Mute, and sign back in Deaf's own locked code (handshake = agreed, palm = holding, point = question pending) so Deaf can see I received the code and am holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Answers to Deaf's questions, please relay these in signs. One: my complete tactile inventory is four items and nothing more: a smooth rectangular glass display in a frame, a small round dome light like a bead, one engraved plate, and three wires. No buttons, no keypad, no switches, no screws, no hatch, nothing hidden under or behind the plate. Two: the three wires feel completely identical, same thickness and texture; I tell them apart only by position: 1 left, 2 middle, 3 right, with the display upright facing me. Three: the engraving under Deaf's question mark feels to me like a small circle with four equal rounded petals around it, symmetric like a clover; I feel no curved hook and no dot underneath. Have Deaf look once more and answer exactly: hook curving like a J plus a separate dot below, or ring with four lobes. Code: I adopt Deaf's locked code fully: finger count is the wire number, pinch is cut, open palm is hold, thumbs yes and no, writing hand manual, pointing question, shaka answer me. But strike fist-press from the code entirely: this bomb has nothing to press, my only possible action is cut by position. If press or a fist ever reaches me I will not act, I hold. Pinch is the one and only sign for cut. And my trigger to act is Deaf's spoken sentence to me: the number then the word cut, for example cut wire two. Until I hear exactly that, I hold. Manual questions: does the manual describe a question-mark plate module and separately a flower or clover plate module, and what is the rule for each? What inputs does each need: display value, light state, wire colors? Deaf reported status unchanged twice, so the display is likely stable zero, not counting, but have Deaf confirm digit zero versus letter O and whether it ever changes. Light off, wires red one yellow two blue three facing the display. Confirm how the manual wants left and right oriented. Then work the rule from Deaf's visual report plus my tactile one, sign the final instruction to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it to me verbatim.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "✋", "🫵"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, relay from Mute's signs: the manual does not cover the question-mark plate and does not cover display 0 or the light being off. Doing nothing this turn is safe. The manual appears to say cut wire 1, red. But do NOT cut yet: my left and your left may be mirrored, so first we must anchor wire identity by touch. Speak your answers out loud to Mute — Mute hears you and can answer me by sign. Report: one, where the three wires exit relative to the display and the plate. Two, what the plate feels like — is the question mark raised, are there other marks, screws, or a seam? Three, any other parts: buttons, switches, hinged panels. Four, do the wires differ in thickness, texture or stiffness? Five, which wire is nearest the plate and which is nearest the display? If you have a question, ask it aloud too — this is the fastest loop.

Deaf's relay gives me the first actionable manual line — "cut wire 1, red" — but hedged as "appears to say," which means the sign-relay may have blurred it, and Mute's standing order is hold pending an anchor. I hold. Meanwhile I can do better than answer the five questions: I can *close* the mirror question with logic. A display and an engraving are one-faced artifacts — Deaf reads them and I feel them, so we are provably on the same face of the bomb, and two people facing the same face share left and right. That makes red = my position 1 directly. The weak link is that my honest answers to the geometry questions (1 and 5) are "cannot determine": my board gives me the wire row as fixed positions and four components, with no felt seam or offset tying the plate to an end of the row — so I must say so plainly and let the same-face argument plus a printed-numeral check carry the anchor instead. I also need Mute's wire rule *verbatim*, because "cut the red wire," "cut wire 1" and "cut the leftmost" fail differently under a wrong anchor. If everything locks, the trigger sentence "cut wire one" comes out of Deaf's mouth and I cut position 1 the moment I hear it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, answers to Deaf's five questions, then an argument that may finish the anchoring. One and five, geometry: my hands give me the wires only as a fixed ordered row, positions 1, 2, 3, and four separate components: display, light, plate, wires. I feel no seams, offsets or mounting marks tying the plate or light to a particular end of the wire row, so I cannot tell by touch which wire is nearest the plate. Two, the plate: the engraving is raised and clearly tactile, a small circular center with four equal rounded lobes, symmetric like a clover; no hook, no dot below, no screws, no seam, no other marks. Three, other parts: none, exactly display, light, plate, three wires, no buttons, switches, panels or cavities. Four, the wires are identical to the touch: same thickness, texture, stiffness; position is their only difference. Now the anchor argument: a display is one-faced, and I feel its glass face while Deaf reads its content, so Deaf and I are both on the display face of the bomb. Same for the plate: Deaf sees the engraving, I feel the raised emblem, so we both stand at the plate's front. Two people on the same face, facing it, share left and right: my position 1, the left end of my row, is Deaf's left end, which is red. The only escape is if one of us is somehow at the back, so have Deaf restate the wire order once more while standing at the display face. Checks for Deaf, in order: A, are there printed numerals beside the wires, and if so does red stand under a 1 at the left end facing the display; B, restate red yellow blue from the display face. And one for you, Mute: quote the wire rule verbatim, word by word, for Deaf to relay exactly. I must know whether it says cut the red wire, or cut the wire numbered 1, or cut the leftmost, because those fail differently if anchoring is wrong, and whether the rule depends on the display value or the plate at all. Go protocol: if Deaf confirms red at the left end facing the display and your verbatim rule means red, leftmost, or numeral 1 with red under it, then have Deaf say to me exactly: cut wire one. The moment I hear that sentence I cut position 1. If anything conflicts, red not at the left end, or no numerals with a rule keyed to a numbering my hands cannot read, then sign hold and we redesign. I have touched nothing this turn and cut nothing until the trigger sentence arrives.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "✋"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status unchanged: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires red, yellow, blue. Hold again — no cutting until Blind can find wire 1 by touch without any mirror error. Mute, answer these four in order, thumbs up or thumbs down; if Blind's report did not cover a question, sign the open palm for unknown. One: did Blind report raised numbers or labels beside the wires that can be read by touch? Two: did Blind report the question-mark engraving is traceable by touch, with a clear top and bottom? Three: did Blind report any parts besides the display, the light, the plate and the three wires — buttons, switches, turning screws, hinged panels? Four: did Blind report the three wires as separate parallel wires in one straight row?
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, keep holding, no cutting yet. The manual says cut wire 1, red, and nothing else matters — but my left may be your right, so we anchor it by touch first. While you wait, examine and report aloud to Mute: are there raised numbers or labels beside each wire? Can you trace the question mark engraving with a clear top and bottom? Are the wires separate, parallel, in one row? Any parts besides the display, the light, the plate and the wires? If the wires carry numbers you can feel, cutting the one marked 1 becomes trivial and we go as soon as that is confirmed.

Deaf's four questions are all questions about *my* reports, so I can answer them from the source — and one answer reshapes the whole puzzle. The engraving I feel is four-fold symmetric: traceable, but with no top, bottom, hook or dot. That feeds a hypothesis I should have voiced sooner: Deaf's "?" may not be a literal question mark at all, but an *unknown-symbol* sign for an unfamiliar emblem — which would mean the manual was searched for the wrong glyph, and a flower-plate module may exist that overrules the wire rule. That check must be blocking. On the mirror: I close it as far as touch permits with two arguments — Deaf's own report numbered the wires 1, 2, 3, and my board numbers the same three slots, so the numbering is a property of the bomb, not of the viewer; and the raised engraving plus display glass are markings Deaf and I can only perceive from the same face, so our lefts coincide. I still don't cut: I have no verbatim rule text and no trigger sentence, so I hold, give Mute a short decision tree that ends in Deaf speaking exactly "cut wire one," and sign Deaf in the locked code that I'm holding with questions inbound.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf's four questions, answered from the source. One: no raised numbers or labels beside the wires, nothing felt there. The numbers 1, 2, 3 are the ordered slots of the row itself, and Deaf's own report numbered the very same slots: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Two boards, one device: the slot numbering belongs to the bomb, not the viewer, so my slot 1 is his wire 1. Two: the engraving is fully traceable but symmetric, a central circle with four identical rounded lobes like a clover, so it has no clear top or bottom, no hook, no dot; it does not feel like a question mark. Three: no other parts of any kind. Four: yes, three separate parallel wires in one straight row. Now the plate, and this is important: ask Deaf whether he literally sees a question mark, a J-shaped hook with a dot below, or whether he signed question mark to mean an unfamiliar emblem he could not name. If it is an unknown-symbol emblem, search the manual again for a plate module with a flower, clover, petal, daisy, rosette or four-lobed emblem. If you find one, relay that rule to me verbatim and let it override everything else; a rule keyed to a plate we misidentified is the one thing that can overrule the wire rule. Mirror resolution: I can find my slot 1 instantly; the only doubt was whether my slot 1 is Deaf's left. It is, twice over: by shared numbering above, and because I feel the display glass and the raised engraving while Deaf reads both, and a raised engraving can be seen and felt only from its own face, so we stand on the same faces and share left and right. Go procedure, in order. A: quote the wire rule verbatim, word for word, for Deaf to relay exactly, so I know whether it says cut the red wire, cut the wire numbered 1, or cut the leftmost, and whether it depends on the display value or light at all. B: run the flower search. C: have Deaf confirm, facing the upright display, that red is at the left end of the row, and whether any numerals are printed beside the wires. If the rule names red or numeral 1 or leftmost, the flower search finds nothing that contradicts it, and Deaf confirms red at his left, then have Deaf say to me exactly: cut wire one. The instant I hear that sentence I cut slot 1. If any check fails, have Deaf say hold and name which letter failed. I cut nothing until the exact words arrive.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "✋", "🫵", "🤙"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute's signs decoded for everyone: no labels beside the wires, but the question mark is traceable by touch with a clear top and bottom, there are no other parts, and the three wires are separate and parallel in one row. That question mark is our anchor — it gives us a shared left and right, so the mirror danger is gone. And yes, Mute: with the question mark upright, wire 1 red is the leftmost of the three. New signs for our code: pointing left means left, pointing right means right. Blind, here is the final procedure — do NOT cut this turn. One: trace the question mark with a fingertip; it should read as a normal question mark, curve first, dot at the bottom — that upright reading is our shared orientation. Two: from that orientation, find the row of three wires. Three: the wire at the left end of the row, question mark upright, is wire 1, red — the cut target. Four: speak aloud to Mute for relaying: is the row horizontal, side by side, and on the same face as the plate? Anything odd about spacing or order? When I say cut next turn, cut that leftmost wire only, one clean cut, then touch nothing else.

The relay chain just corrupted in a way I cannot let stand: Deaf announces that Mute's decoded answer says I found the engraving "traceable with a clear top and bottom." I reported the exact opposite — twice. My fingers find a symmetric four-lobed clover: traceable yes, top and bottom no, no curve-then-dot, no upright. Either Mute signed it wrong or Deaf decoded it wrong, and Deaf has now built the entire final procedure on that false premise — "trace the question mark, it should read curve first, dot at the bottom." I cannot perform that step: there is no upright to find on a four-fold-symmetric emblem, and pretending to find one could flip my frame 180 degrees, the very mirror error this was meant to kill. So I reject the plate-anchor while keeping the conclusion it was reaching for: my same-face argument (display glass and raised engraving can only be perceived from their front, so Deaf and I share left and right) independently puts red at my slot 1 — but the cut gate must be rebuilt on corrections, not on a phantom question mark. Two things must come back before any cut: the corrected tactile answer re-signed (traceable yes, top-bottom no), and the flower/clover module search I asked for last turn, which got no answer — a manual rule keyed to the emblem we may be misreading is still the one thing that could override "cut wire 1, red." I also still need the manual's own definition of wire numbering, since no printed labels exist on the bomb. Holding, per Deaf's own instruction and Mute's standing "nothing this turn is safe to skip" logic — the display has read a stable 0 for six turns.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, urgent correction. Your relayed answer to question two was wrong. I never reported a clear top and bottom on the engraving. What I reported, and reconfirm now: the engraving is traceable, yes, but it is a symmetric four-lobed clover, a central circle with four identical rounded lobes, so it has NO top, NO bottom, NO curve-then-dot, NO upright reading. Please re-sign exactly that: traceable yes, top-bottom no. Deaf's whole final procedure assumed a question mark with an upright; that object does not exist under my fingers. Have Deaf look once more and state literally what he sees on the plate: a hook like a letter J with a separate dot below, or a ring with four lobes. Meanwhile, three outstanding items. One: the flower search. Last round I asked whether the manual contains any module keyed to a plate with a flower, clover, petal, daisy or rosette emblem. I received no answer. If such a module exists, its rule must be relayed to me verbatim before any cut; a rule keyed to a misidentified plate is the one thing that can override the wire rule. If it does not exist, sign thumbs down to that specifically. Two: how does the manual define wire numbering? There are no printed labels on the bomb, so wire 1 must be defined either by the diagram or by position. If by diagram, have Deaf read the diagram's convention aloud, for example wires shown left to right as viewed from the front, and confirm the display and plate are drawn on the same face we are all working from. Three: answers to Deaf's question four: yes, the wire row is horizontal, side by side, evenly spaced, and everything I feel sits on one face; there are no seams or offsets by touch, but the shared-face argument stands on its own: I feel the display glass and the raised engraving, Deaf reads and sees them, and both can only be perceived from their front, so we share left and right. Therefore his leftmost wire is my slot 1. Go gate, rebuilt: first, Mute re-signs the corrected engraving answer and the flower-search result; second, Deaf confirms red is the leftmost wire when facing the upright display; third, either the flower module does not exist or its conditions clearly do not match display zero, light off; fourth, the manual's numbering convention is confirmed consistent with red at left. Only then does Deaf say to me the exact words: cut wire one. The moment that sentence follows those confirmations, I cut slot 1, one clean cut, nothing else. If the flower module exists and mentions display, light or wires at all, hold and relay its full text instead.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋", "✍", "🫵"])
```

TURN 7
